findings.body: The computed translation includes the user-controlled `model.fancyTitle` and is inserted with triple-stash rendering, allowing markup in the title to become executable HTML on the unsubscribe page.
findings.failure_mode: A malicious topic title can produce stored cross-site scripting for users who visit the unsubscribe page.
findings.impact: The computed translation includes the user-controlled `model.fancyTitle` and is inserted with triple-stash rendering, allowing markup in the title to become executable HTML on the unsubscribe page.
findings.root_cause: The entire translated string, including interpolated topic-title content, is rendered as raw HTML.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the title through a normally escaped template expression and keep only trusted translation markup outside it, or explicitly HTML-escape the title before passing it to the translation.
findings.title: Escape the topic title before rendering the translated message
findings.trigger: A topic title contains HTML such as an element with an event handler, and a logged-in recipient opens that topic's unsubscribe URL.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R3 shows `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` using triple-stash (raw HTML) rendering. The controller at line R6 interpolates `model.fancyTitle` (user-controlled topic title) into the translation. This creates stored XSS when a topic title contains malicious HTML.

findings.body: `find_by` returns nil and the following `tu.notification_level` dereference raises, returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing the recipient.
findings.failure_mode: The unsubscribe endpoint crashes for valid users without a topic-specific preference record.
findings.impact: `find_by` returns nil and the following `tu.notification_level` dereference raises, returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing the recipient.
findings.root_cause: The action assumes a per-topic user record exists for every email recipient.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `TopicUser.change` or create/find a TopicUser record before reading or updating its notification level; this also preserves the normal notification-change bookkeeping.
findings.title: Handle recipients that do not yet have a TopicUser row
findings.trigger: A recipient notified through a category-level setting or a mention opens the link before ever creating a `topic_users` row for that topic.
findings.verifier_reason: Line R105 shows `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` which returns nil if no record exists. Line R107 immediately calls `tu.notification_level` without nil check, causing NoMethodError. Users notified via category settings may lack TopicUser rows.
